title: Reasoning primer: syllogisms and the fallacies that imitate them
question: Which of these arguments actually deduce their conclusions — and which only look like they do?
description: A teaching case for the Reasoning Explorer. Classic valid forms (Barbara, modus ponens, hypothetical syllogism, a two-step chain) sit beside the formal fallacies that imitate them (affirming the consequent, denying the antecedent, undistributed middle, equivocation) and one inductive leap. Every term is a defined concept, so both engines — KnowShowGo's rule-based inference core and the native forward-chaining prover — can show their work.
